cues.zh: 所以现在，无论你在网络中的哪个位置，你都知道该怎么处理这玩意儿。你知道它是不是给你的。你知道它要去哪里，所以你能想办法把它送到那儿。所以把隐式信息显式化，突然就能支持一堆新功能、新用例。这很容易搞砸。所以当电信运营商搞 ATM 网络时，他们在 54 字节的小信元里放了标识符，但他们用的是

cues.en: this local identifier, it only had meaning to the two switches on each end of a wire. It was rewritten on every hop. So you got this thing which got rid of the time slot assignment on a trunk, but it had no value at all in terms of the system characteristics. It didn't make anything more reliable. It didn't let the destination switch fix anything up, because it still had this number which had no meaning except for the wire the data came in on. It had no larger context.
cues.zh: 这个本地标识符，它只对一条链路两端的两个交换机有意义。它在每一跳都会被重写。所以你有了这个东西，它摆脱了干线上的时隙分配，但在系统特性方面毫无价值。它没有让任何东西更可靠。它也没让目的交换机做任何修复，因为它仍然只有这个编号，除了数据进来的那条链路之外毫无意义。它没有更大的上下文。

cues.en: So you give a few milliseconds thought to this problem, because you don't want to screw it up. But you do the analogous thing in dissemination, where you take information that's implicit, like time information or version information. You say, oh, if I'm connected to sourceforge.net, then the version of GNOME that I'm pulling over is the most recent GNOME, because this is the master repository. Instead, you put the version.
cues.zh: 所以你会花几毫秒想想这个问题，因为不想把它搞砸。但在分发时你会做类似的事：把隐式信息，比如时间信息或版本信息，拿出来。你会说，哦，如果我连到 sourceforge.net，那我拉取的 GNOME 版本就是最新的 GNOME，因为这是主仓库。相反，你把版本

cues.en: information explicitly, you have something that tells you what the most recent version is, and you request that version. There's some harder stuff to do. If you want to do a world scale network on this, you've got to work out the incentive structure, which is the equivalent of TCP's congestion control. You've got to make sure that people get everything they need, but they don't shut out other people. So they get some kind of fair share.
cues.zh: 信息显式化：你有个东西能告诉你最新版本是什么，然后你请求那个版本。还有一些更难的事。如果想在这个基础上做全球规模的网络，你得设计好激励机制，相当于 TCP 的拥塞控制。你得确保人们拿到所需的一切，但又不会把别人排除在外，让他们也能得到某种公平份额。

cues.en: Since anything can both source and sync data, you want to really drive the bit torrent ideas of you should redistribute content. And it's in your interest to redistribute content, because you'll get it faster if you agree to get people to other. If you're going to use people riding their bicycle across Africa as a communication mechanism to network the third world, you really want a lot of incentive on data sharing.
cues.zh: 既然任何东西都能作为数据源并同步数据，你就要真正推动 BitTorrent 那套理念：内容应该被再分发。而且再分发内容符合你的利益，因为如果你同意把内容传给其他人，你自己也能更快拿到。如果你打算把骑车穿越非洲的人当作通信机制，去为第三世界组网，那你就真的需要对数据共享设置很强的激励。

cues.en: You can build that into the flow control. BitTorrent's done a bit of it. In all the peer-to-peer systems, you have a tremendous problem with miscreants and freeloaders. People are dumping in bogus content, taking but not giving back. You want to architect that out at the network level. You want to make that as hard as possible.
cues.zh: 你可以把这一点构建进流控里。BitTorrent 已经做了一部分。在所有 P2P 系统里，你都会遇到恶意用户和搭便车者这个大问题。人们会灌入虚假内容，只下载不上传。你要在网络层面通过架构把它排除掉。你要让这件事尽可能难。

cues.en: exactly how you do content routing, what the policies are for redistribution. You get some stuff that you really didn't ask for, but you're going to carry it along in case somebody else wants it. I mean, that's fine. My phone's got four gig, of which three gig are empty. I'm happy to carry some extra data, spread it out in the world. But exactly what do I carry? What's likely to be useful where I'm going? Or do I just grab everything that's in my environment?
cues.zh: 内容路由到底怎么做，再分发策略又是什么。你会拿到一些自己根本没要的东西，但也会随身带着，以防别人需要。我是说，这没问题。我手机有 4GB，其中 3GB 是空的。我愿意多带点数据，把它传播到世界各处。但到底该带什么？我要去的地方哪些可能有用？还是环境里有什么就全抓走？

cues.en: And then there's liability issues. What if one of the things I'm carrying is a virus? And it comes back to me and say, oh, I'm going to sue your pants off because you gave me this virus. I go, hey, it was encrypted. I didn't even know. So when you're architecting, you want to architect around those issues or look at the legal ramifications. And then you've got this content that either deliberately or accidentally is going to get corrupted. And you don't want to be checking.
cues.zh: 然后是责任问题。如果我带的东西里有病毒怎么办？然后它回来找我，说，哦，我要告到你倾家荡产，因为你把这个病毒给了我。我说，嘿，它是加密的，我根本不知道。所以做架构时，你要在架构上绕开这些问题，或者考虑法律后果。然后还有这些内容，迟早会被故意或意外损坏。你也不想一直去检查。

cues.en: every piece of content everywhere as it's flowing through the world. So you would like a system where you can mostly distribute content, but if somebody says, hey, that copy of GCC that you gave me was completely bogus, you want to be able to go back up the distribution path and nuke that copy so that you don't hand it on to poor unsuspecting people. And there are gossip and reputation and epidemic systems that do that kind of lazy invalidation. So I think we can work that out.
cues.zh: 世界上流动的每一份内容。所以你希望有一个系统，让你主要可以分发内容，但如果有人说：“嘿，你给我的那份 GCC 完全是假的”，你希望能沿着分发路径回溯，并把那份副本销毁，这样就不会再把它传给毫不知情的人。而且有流言、声誉和流行病式系统来做这种惰性失效。所以我觉得我们可以把这个问题解决掉。

cues.en: When we were working out problems like this on the original internet, I tried to phrase this in a way that would be acceptable to Republicans as well, but there's no intelligent design in the network. It was just sort of hooked up. So we actually had this evolutionary force, which was the evil empire, and they were going to bomb the daylights out of us, and we wanted to make a network that would survive that.
cues.zh: 当年我们在最初的互联网上解决这类问题时，我试着用一种共和党人也能接受的说法来表达，但网络里并没有什么智能设计。它只是被连起来而已。所以我们其实有一股进化力量，也就是邪恶帝国，他们要把我们炸得稀巴烂，而我想造一个能在那样的打击下存活的网络。

cues.en: And that really clarifies your thinking. It gives you a way to test all your design decisions and say, OK, well, if they drop the bomb, is this going to work? Do we have states spread out through the universe, or is it concentrated and nicely distributed? Do we have routing information? What's happening? So you look around and say, OK, if I were doing a new network today, the evil empire is gone.
cues.zh: 这确实能让你的思路更清晰。它让你能检验所有设计决策，然后问：好，如果他们把炸弹扔下来，这还能行吗？我们的状态是散布在整个宇宙里，还是集中起来并妥善分布？我们有路由信息吗？到底会发生什么？所以你环顾四周说：好，如果我今天要做一个新网络，邪恶帝国已经没了。

cues.en: It moved to Washington. But what do we have that's an equivalent? And I say, there's lots. We've got an epidemic of greed. There have been five generations of peer-to-peer systems. They've all gotten better. They've all gone from very centralized ideas, centralized names, centralized content, to very distributed names, distributed content. It's all been basically driven by these guys in their endless lawsuits. So it's great.
cues.zh: 它搬到华盛顿去了。但我们有什么对等物呢？我说，有很多。我们正处在贪婪泛滥之中。点对点系统已经历了五代。它们都越变越好。它们都从非常集中式的想法、集中式命名、集中式内容，转向了高度分布式的命名、分布式内容。这基本上都是被这帮人无休止的官司推着走的。所以这很棒。

cues.en: There's a lot of drivers that I think will help us make the right kind of content network. So I'm finally done. So TCPIP is a huge advance. We no longer had to plumb up our connections. But now, 30 years on, we've evolved to the point where now we have to do plumbing at the data level in order to get the data we want in the places we need it.
cues.zh: 我认为有很多推动因素能帮我们构建合适的内容网络。我终于讲完了。TCP/IP 是巨大的进步。我们不再需要手动接通连接。但 30 年过去了，我们已经发展到必须在数据层做连接，才能把想要的数据送到需要的地方。

cues.en: We have to do a bunch of low-level connection plumbing. If you move your view of networking to the data level, change your point of view, a dissemination architecture says, no, let the network do the plumbing like it should. This is being done. I'm not talking about anything revolutionary. The work's going on. It just seems to me to be sort of fragmented in ad hoc. But there's Akamai, there's BitTorrent, Sonos is selling music players that you just sort of set up.
cues.zh: 我们得做一堆底层的连接铺设工作。如果把网络视角移到数据层，换个角度看，分发架构会说：不，让网络按它该有的方式去做连接。这件事正在发生。我说的不是什么革命性的事。这项工作正在进行。只是在我看来，它有点零散、临时。但有 Akamai，有 BitTorrent，Sonos 在卖那种你稍微设置一下就能用的音乐播放器。

cues.en: It's spreading music around. Apple's got this nice rendezvous system for getting at resources and various kinds of information. So I think there's a demonstration need. There's lots of emotion. And lastly, we're killing so many brains in academia. It's like we wasted.
cues.zh: 它在四处传播音乐。Apple 有一套很好的 rendezvous 系统，用来访问资源和各类信息。所以我觉得有必要做个演示。这里面有很多情绪。最后，我们在学术界扼杀了太多大脑。就像我们在浪费。

cues.en: 20 years of grad students having them work on circuit switching, and now we've wasted 20 years of grad students having them working on replacing TCPIP. Don't replace it. Use it. Do something new. And so I'd like to kind of push the world to a different point of view. And I'm done. Questions? So I'm supposed to repeat the questions. What do I think of BitTorrent as a solution, and what problems does A?
cues.zh: 20 年来，研究生一直在做电路交换；现在我们又浪费了 20 年，让研究生去替换 TCP/IP。别替换它。用它。做点新东西。所以我想把世界推向另一种视角。我说完了。有问题吗？我得重复一下问题。我怎么看 BitTorrent 作为一种解决方案，以及 A 有什么问题？

cues.en: does it have? It's sort of a long discussion, but the biggest issue is the temporal binding when you're doing the torrent distribution. So your client talks to a tracker, basically gets a list of other clients that are busy downloading this content, and can talk to those other clients and get pieces that they've already got in addition to getting some pieces from the tracker.
cues.zh: 它有哪些问题？这个问题说来话长，但最大的问题是做 torrent 分发时的时间绑定。你的客户端会和 tracker 通信，基本上拿到一份正在下载这个内容的其他客户端列表，然后就能和这些客户端通信，从它们那里拿到已经有的分片，同时也能从 tracker 拿到一些分片。

cues.en: There isn't any fixed distributed memory in the system. The only people that are eligible to give you the content are ones that are getting it themselves. And that means it only works for big content. So what you see going over torrent is movies and the latest KDE distribution. Big honk on things, because the individual downloads have to last long enough so that you have a big population of other downloaders on which to draw.
cues.zh: 这个系统里没有任何固定的分布式存储。只有那些自己正在获取内容的人，才有资格把内容提供给你。这意味着它只适用于大内容。所以你在 torrent 上看到的是电影和最新的 KDE 发行版。都是些大块头，因为单个下载必须持续够久，才能积累出大量其他下载者可供利用。

cues.en: Because the protocols that you use to get them are entirely topology unaware, your initial seed might be anywhere. The initial downloaders might be anywhere. You do some statistics as you're downloading and preferentially use ones that are close to you topologically. But there's nothing in the protocol that can set that up. It can't do any learning. It can't use any location information, because basically it doesn't have a way of distributing the trackers.
cues.zh: 因为你用来获取它们的协议完全不感知拓扑，你的初始种子可能在任何地方。最初的下载者也可能在任何地方。你会在下载时做一些统计，优先选用拓扑上离你近的节点。但协议里没有任何机制能建立这种关系。它不能做任何学习。它不能用任何位置信息，因为基本上它没有办法分发 tracker。

cues.en: And if it did try to distributing trackers, you'd be in the Nutella world where you never know when to forget everything. Everyone who ever asked for this content is registered as a possible source of the content. And so you've got 10 billion places to get it from, most of which are unreachable. And when you do a content distribution network, you still have to think about locality.
cues.zh: 而且如果它真的尝试分发 tracker，你就会进入 Nutella 世界：永远不知道该在什么时候忘掉一切。每个曾经请求过这个内容的人，都会被登记为该内容的可能来源。于是你有 100 亿个位置可以取内容，其中大多数不可达。做内容分发网络时，你仍然要考虑本地性。

cues.en: Eventually, you want to be able to get stuff from anywhere on the planet, but get it closed first. And that requires really architecting how the requests happen. But you can't do it with something like BitTorrent. You don't have control of that level of the infrastructure.
cues.zh: 最终，你希望能从地球上任何地方获取内容，但首先要让它离得近。而这需要真正设计好请求是如何发生的。但用 BitTorrent 这类东西做不到。你控制不了那一层的基础设施。

cues.en: So I think the question was, I talked about broadcast. What do I think of IP multicast? I love IP multicast. It made many things easy when we were doing the voice and video tools. And it's sort of an experience that underlays a lot of the thoughts about dissemination. If you've got multicast.
cues.zh: 所以我想问题是，我谈到了广播。我怎么看 IP 组播？我很喜欢 IP 组播。当年我们做语音和视频工具时，它让很多事情变得容易。而且它是一种经验，支撑了很多关于传播的思考。如果你有组播的话。

cues.en: universally available, then you don't think about conversations anymore. You think more about disseminations with conversations being a limiting, just a two party case. But as you say, you can't scale it up. You can't make it global. My feeling is you shouldn't have to, that if you're thinking at that level, you're thinking too far down. That you want to think about the data and where you are right now, what's the good way to ask your questions and get your answers.
cues.zh: 一旦普遍可用，你就不再考虑对话了。你会更多考虑分发，而对话只是一种受限的、仅限双方的情形。但如你所说，你没法把它扩展上去。你没法让它覆盖全球。我的感觉是，你本不该需要这么做；如果你在那个层面思考，那就是想得太底层了。你应该关注数据和你当前所在的位置，关注怎样提问并得到答案才是好办法。

cues.en: And so if you've got room level link layer broadcast, that's great. If you've got enterprise level IP multicast, that's great. And you don't need it in the world. Because what you're trying to do is to get some copies of the data that are close to you or get the data closer to you. And so it's kind of, I think, like web proxy auto discovery.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你有房间级链路层广播，那很好。如果你有企业级 IP 组播，那也很好。你并不需要它在全球范围内可用。因为你想做的是拿到一些离你近的数据副本，或者让数据离你更近。所以我觉得，这有点像 Web Proxy Auto Discovery。

cues.en: I can multicast a URL inside of Google, and that's going to hit the closest proxy, which will either give me the data or it will go fetch it. And if it goes fetches it, then it's got it. And so if somebody else has asked, they'll get the data from the proxy. And finding that proxy by a multicast, resolving DNS names by a multicast is very efficient, because you can use the media efficiently.
cues.zh: 我可以在 Google 内部对一个 URL 做组播，请求会打到最近的代理，代理要么直接给我数据，要么去把数据取回来。如果它去取，那它就拿到了。所以如果别人也请求过，就能直接从代理拿到数据。而且用组播找到那个代理、用组播解析 DNS 名字非常高效，因为可以高效地利用介质。

cues.en: Topological awareness is buried in the network, so you don't get multiple copies of the data going over one link. And because the behavior is sort of like cache replacement semantics, the only thing that's unicast are the misses. So as you're pulling the data down, yeah, so one request went unicast, but the next 99 went multicast.
cues.zh: 拓扑感知被埋在网络里，所以同一份数据不会在一条链路上传输多份。而且因为它的行为有点像缓存替换语义，只有未命中才会走单播。所以当你把数据拉下来时，没错，第一个请求走了单播，但接下来 99 个都走了组播。

cues.en: And I think if you architect the system, so it's got that kind of behavior. So as data diffuses from producers to consumers, then you get more of the cash locality semantics. And that means that you only need local multicast. And we should do a local multicast.
cues.zh: 而且我认为，如果你这样设计系统架构，它就会具备那种行为。这样当数据从生产者扩散到消费者时，你就能获得更多缓存局部性语义。这意味着你只需要本地多播。而且我们应该做本地多播。
